items.title: Storage accounting and retention cleanup
acceptance: Reported usage agrees with database/files
Retention cleanup reconciles orphan files
Failures visible with safe retry
evidence: Commit c1cd371: declarative partition storage includes descendant heap/index/TOAST; ordinary inheritance counted once. Blob errors preserve rows unless confirmed missing under available root; UUID/day paths reject static symlinks; all thumbnail filesystem work retains lifecycle lease and falls back to already-read original bytes.

Reviewed server verification: 118 regular tests plus 32 PostgreSQL tests passed (150 total), strict Clippy, formatting and diff checks passed. PostgreSQL used a fresh disposable container and temporary fixtures; container removed.

Commit 73a4ff7: bounded retryable Recall cleanup uses shared device lifecycle gates and confirmed database reference absence; static symlinks rejected, active blocking workers retain gates after cancellation, and malformed partition names cannot starve valid batches.

Reviewed full server verification: 161 tests passed (123 regular +38 temporary PostgreSQL), including 11 new retention filesystem/concurrency/DB cases; strict all-target Clippy, formatting and whitespace pass; disposable PostgreSQL container removed.
limitations: Database accounting excludes JPEG/thumbnail/WAL/backup bytes. Values are approximate catalog reads, not a frozen disk snapshot.
Default-partition row pruning is delegated; per-file orphan reclamation within indexed days and backup restore remain pending. No real storage scan, cleanup or restore was performed.

Cleanup is bounded to four partition drops, 512 scanned entries and 32 candidate days per pass; full reconciliation can take multiple scan cycles/intervals. Unindexed reference checks may limit throughput.
Static path checks assume trusted local storage against external replacement; gates coordinate one server process. Non-abortable filesystem work retains gates beyond timeout.

items.title: Backup restore and diagnostic tools
acceptance: Backup restored into clean instance and verified

evidence: Commit 2f6c88b: metadata-only diagnostic JSON with allowlisted OS/architecture, repository commit/tracked dirty state, fixed parsed tool versions and optional aggregate disk capacity. No configuration/log/content/identifier/path values; output files exclusively created with private permissions.
Fourteen tests passed in delegate and root runs, including actual local processes for noisy/trickling output, deadlines, normal exit and descendant-held stdout; POSIX process groups cleaned up.
limitations: Backup restore remains planned and unverified; diagnostic metadata does not establish server health or recovery.

Windows pipe and descendant behavior are not platform verified; direct child cleanup is implemented without a Job Object. Git dirty state excludes untracked files and submodules; sanitized system PATH may report user-installed tools unavailable.
